props.title: Once Upon A Mattress
props.initialSlug: A royal rumble fit for a queen!

sections.content: **Once Upon a Mattress** (2005) reimagines the classic fairy tale "The Princess and the Pea" with Carol Burnett switching roles from her 1972 television version - this time playing the devious Queen Aggravain instead of Princess Winnifred. The film follows the tradition of musical adaptations like **Rogers & Hammerstein's Cinderella** (1957, remade 1997) and **The Wonderful World of Disney**'s **Once Upon a Time** (2011) series in modernizing fairy tales for contemporary audiences. Director Kathleen Marshall, known for her Broadway work, brings theatrical flair while maintaining the story's medieval setting.

sections.content: The 2005 version particularly shines in its comedic elements, with Tracey Ullman taking over Burnett's former role as the unrefined Princess Winnifred. The production follows Disney's successful formula of updating classic stories seen in **Enchanted** (2007) and **Maleficent** (2014), though maintaining more theatrical roots. The musical numbers retain their Broadway energy while adapting to the television format, similar to how **Annie** (1999) and **The Music Man** (2003) translated stage classics to TV. SUBHEAD: Modern Fairy Tale Adaptations

This adaptation sits within a larger trend of fairy tale reinventions that gained momentum in the 2000s. While **Once Upon a Mattress** (2005) keeps its playful tone, later adaptations like **Snow White and the Huntsman** (2012) and **Mirror Mirror** (2012) took darker approaches. The film's strength lies in balancing traditional elements with contemporary humor, much like **Ella Enchanted** (2004) and **A Cinderella Story** (2004).
